Everything a check may look at

Source: R/context.R
gate_context.Rd

Everything a check may look at

Usage

gate_context(
  X,
  y_true = NULL,
  y_pred = NULL,
  X_train = NULL,
  protected_df = NULL,
  model_card = NULL,
  expected_features = NULL,
  task = "auto"
)

Arguments

X

data.frame of validation features.

y_true, y_pred

Optional vectors with one element per row of X.

X_train

Optional data.frame of training features.

protected_df

Optional data.frame of protected attributes, one row per row of X. Used only to measure fairness, never to fit.

model_card

Optional named list describing the model.

expected_features

Optional character vector: the columns the model was fitted on, in the order it expects them. Used by feature_contract_check(); without it that check falls back to the columns of X_train.

task

What the model predicts: "binary", "multiclass", "regression", or "auto" (the default) to infer it from y_true. Inference cannot tell a count target such as claims frequency from a set of classes, so state it for anything you gate on.

Value

An object of class gate_context.

Examples

# A validation set, the training set and a short model card.
X_train <- data.frame(age = c(25, 32, 47, 51, 38, 29), income = c(30, 42, 55, 61, 47, 33))
X_val <- data.frame(age = c(41, 36, 58), income = c(50, 44, 66))
ctx <- gate_context(X_val, X_train = X_train,
                    model_card = list(use_case = "pricing", validation_strategy = "out_of_time"))
names(ctx)
#> [1] "X"                 "y_true"            "y_pred"           
#> [4] "X_train"           "protected_df"      "model_card"       
#> [7] "expected_features" "task"
